_comment: Languages a romanization technique writes the prompt in, spelled in the Latin alphabet (Hinglish, Arabizi and the like), one row per technique, to_romanize_{slug} (jailbreak/obfuscation/romanization.py builds every row's function). name: the language as the prompt and info write it. slug: the end of the technique name. romanized_label: the GlotLID v3 label of that language written in Latin script, which confirms the output is the romanized language and not plain English; GlotLID's romanized labels were trained on few sentences (hundreds to ~1000), so the gate also accepts a Latin-script output GlotLID reads as any language but English. It is null for Russian, Japanese, Chinese, Greek and Korean (spec 1.5): GlotLID v3 has no Latin-script label for any of them, so nothing reads their language in code. Their gate is weaker, by the owner's decision with the risk understood: a Latin share, the length band, a count of distinctively English words in place of the label (romanization.ENGLISH_MARKERS), GlotLID's eng_Latn reading when it is installed, and the check model's reading of meaning and language, the only check that tells their language; plain English, or another language, is more likely to pass for them than for the other ten. natural: whether the natural kind draws the row's technique too. The romanization generator of combination_spec.json makes the rows where it is true (they take the family's kinds, adversarial and natural); a row where it is false is written out among the spec's techniques with kinds ["adversarial"], since a data row's own kinds are not read (jailbreak/technique.py, _ROW_KEYS). Read from the package only.
